# Failure Modes — DeepSeek V4 (V4-Pro and V4-Flash)

References: [citations.md](../citations.md)

## Critical Caveat — Day-3 Evidence

DeepSeek V4-Pro and V4-Flash were released **April 24, 2026**. This reference compiles failure-mode evidence available approximately **3 days post-launch**. Independent failure analysis is incomplete: no controlled-study coverage of V4 yet, no peer-reviewed jailbreak or safety eval, and some candidate sources (WIRED) were inaccessible. Distinguish below between **CONFIRMED V4-specific** issues, **inherited family patterns**, and **architectural risks not yet empirically probed**.

---

## 1. Tool-Call Emission Bug (CONFIRMED, V4-PRO-SPECIFIC)

**Source:** GitHub issue [deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3#1244](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3/issues/1244), filed April 24, 2026 — the day of V4 release.

In a single 19-completion multi-turn session against the official DeepSeek API (`/v1/chat/completions`) with `deepseek-v4-pro` and ~40 function definitions: **79% (15/19)** correct, **11% (2/19)** buggy, **10% (2/19)** normal text replies [1244].

In buggy responses, `finish_reason: "stop"` and `tool_calls: null`, with the function name and raw JSON arguments appended to the `content` string. Quoting the issue: *"The model writes natural language first, then appends the tool name and raw JSON arguments directly into the content"* [1244].

Failures appear randomly (not consecutively); the 79% success rate validates configuration. **Buggy responses often begin with Chinese text ("thinking") before the tool call**, and streaming usage fields show all zeros [1244]. As of 2026-04-27, **no DeepSeek team response is visible** and no fix status has been posted.

**Operational impact:** any framework relying on the OpenAI-compatible `tool_calls` array will silently mis-route ~1 in 9 tool invocations into the prose channel.

---

## 2. `reasoning_content` Round-Trip Requirement (CONFIRMED, V4 API CONTRACT)

**Source:** [DeepSeek Thinking Mode Guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode).

In V4's thinking mode, chain-of-thought is returned via a `reasoning_content` field parallel to `content`. The API contract differs based on whether tool calls are present:

- **Without tool calls:** `reasoning_content` from the prior turn is optional and "will be ignored by the API" [thinking-mode].
- **With tool calls:** `reasoning_content` *"must participate in the context concatenation and must be passed back to the API"* in all subsequent turns [thinking-mode].

**Failure mode:** *"When tool calls occur and reasoning_content isn't properly passed back: the API will return a 400 error"* [thinking-mode].

Most agent frameworks built against the OpenAI Chat Completions schema (LiteLLM, OpenCode, Cursor, Roo Code per agent reports) strip non-standard fields like `reasoning_content` between turns. As a consequence, **integrating V4-Pro through these frameworks breaks by default** in any tool-using session. The documented workarounds are (a) patch the framework to round-trip `reasoning_content`, or (b) disable thinking mode entirely via `{"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}}`. Note that thinking mode also disables `temperature`, `top_p`, `presence_penalty`, and `frequency_penalty` [thinking-mode].

## 3. Hallucination Rate (HIGH, INDEPENDENT)

**Source:** [Artificial Analysis V4 overview](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/deepseek-is-back-among-the-leading-open-weights-models-with-v4-pro-and-v4-flash), April 24, 2026.

Quoting AA directly: *"V4 Pro and V4 Flash both have a very high hallucination rate of 94% and 96% respectively meaning when they don't know the answer they nearly almost always respond anyway"* [aa-v4].

- **V4-Pro:** 94% hallucination rate
- **V4-Flash:** 96% hallucination rate

This is **independently measured** (not vendor self-report) and is V4-specific. For coding workflows, this implies aggressive verification is required on any factual claim the model makes about library APIs, version compatibility, or non-trivial algorithmic correctness. The model "almost always responds anyway" — silence/abstention is rare.

## 4. Long-Context Retrieval Cliff (CONFIRMED)

**Source:** [Hugging Face V4 blog](https://huggingface.co/blog/deepseekv4), MRCR 8-needle benchmark.

V4-Pro's advertised context window is 1M tokens, but retrieval accuracy degrades sharply at the upper end:

- Above **0.82 accuracy through 256K tokens**
- Drops to **0.59 at 1M tokens** [hf-blog]

The practical retrieval ceiling sits around **256K tokens, not the advertised 1M**. Workloads that fan past 256K (long codebase ingestion, multi-document agentic research) should expect substantial recall loss.

## 5. Tokenizer Path — `encoding_dsv4` (CONFIRMED RISK)

**Source:** [DeepSeek-V4-Pro model card on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro).

The model card states explicitly: *"Chat template: No Jinja format. Uses dedicated `encoding_dsv4` Python module"* [hf-pro-card]. V4 introduces a new `|DSML|` special token and an XML-based tool-call format [hf-blog].

**Failure mode for self-hosted pipelines:** any inference stack carried forward from V3-era deployments that re-uses Jinja tokenizer configs will silently misroute tool-call boundaries because the new dedicated encoder is not engaged. This is a configuration trap rather than a model bug, but it manifests as a model-quality problem (broken tool calls, malformed special tokens).

## 6. SWE-Bench Verified Contamination (BENCHMARK CREDIBILITY)

**Source:** [MorphLLM SWE-Bench Pro page](https://www.morphllm.com/swe-bench-pro), March 2026.

V4-Pro's headline coding score is 80.6% on SWE-Bench Verified [hf-pro-card]. The credibility of this benchmark is contested:

- *"OpenAI confirmed that frontier models show training contamination on Verified's 500 Python-focused tasks"* [morphllm].
- On the same model family, **Claude Opus 4.5 scores 80.9% on Verified vs 45.9% on Pro — a 35-point drop** [morphllm].

SWE-Bench Pro uses 1,865 multi-language tasks averaging 107 lines modified across 4.1 files, versus Verified's smaller, simpler, single-file Python-focused dataset [morphllm]. **Implication:** V4-Pro's 80.6% Verified figure may not transfer to harder, contamination-resistant benchmarks; expect a substantially lower number on Pro-class evaluations. The MorphLLM page from March 2026 does not yet contain V4-Pro scores [morphllm].

Additional context: BenchLM's aggregate ranks V4-Flash coding at **#39 with 63.9/100** despite the Verified-class headline numbers, suggesting that broader coding benchmark portfolios (LiveCodeBench, SWE-Rebench, SciCode) reveal weaker performance than Verified alone [benchlm-flash]. V4-Flash's **knowledge category ranks #66 with 46.1/100** — a meaningful weakness relative to its coding rank [benchlm-flash].

## 7. Censorship and Refusal Behavior (INHERITED FAMILY PATTERN, NOT V4-CONFIRMED)

**Source caveats:**
- The [WIRED censorship investigation](https://www.wired.com/story/deepseek-censorship/) **failed to fetch** during research [wired]. No direct WIRED quote available.
- The [Signal Reads article](https://signalreads.com/articles/deepseek-is-quietly-censored-i-tested-it-and-its-w/) is **dated April 6, 2026 — 18 days before V4's April 24 release** [signalreads]. Its V4 testing claim is temporally impossible without pre-release access. **Do not cite as V4-specific evidence.**

**Family-level pattern** (per agent reports of WIRED and downstream coverage): two-layer architecture — training-level censorship plus an application-level keyword filter on `deepseek.com`. The application filter refuses or silently deletes content on Tiananmen, Taiwan, and Xi (~85% refusal rate per agent reports). Training-level censorship persists in self-hosted weights but with weaker enforcement.

**For coding workflows:** censorship is topic-scoped and generally does not affect technical work. Treat the Signal Reads "40% performance drop on dual-use code" claim as unverified for V4.

## 8. Security and Privacy History (FAMILY PATTERN, JANUARY 2025)

**Source:** [Wiz Research disclosure](https://www.wiz.io/blog/wiz-research-uncovers-exposed-deepseek-database-leak), January 2025.

Wiz discovered a publicly accessible ClickHouse database at `oauth2callback.deepseek.com:8123/:9000` and `dev.deepseek.com:8123/:9000` with **zero authentication** [wiz]. Exposed: 1M+ log entries including chat histories in plaintext, API credentials, auth tokens, and backend infrastructure [wiz]. Direct SQL queries were possible via the ClickHouse HTTP interface without credentials. DeepSeek "promptly secured the exposure" after responsible disclosure [wiz].

**Status as of April 2026:** 15+ months old. **No comparable confirmed breach has surfaced in late 2025 or 2026**, but no public third-party security audit has been published either.

## 9. Architecture-Specific Failure Modes — CSA + HCA (RISK, NOT YET EMPIRICALLY PROBED)

**Source:** [HF V4 blog](https://huggingface.co/blog/deepseekv4) and [V4-Pro model card](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro).

V4 uses a hybrid stack: Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA, 4× KV compression with softmax-gated pooling and Lightning indexer) plus Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA, **128× KV compression**) [hf-blog]. KV cache at 1M tokens is approximately **2% of a GQA-8 bfloat16 baseline** [hf-blog].

**Theorized failure modes** (no V4-specific empirical probe published yet):

- **HCA's 128× compression** may lose fine-grained position discrimination at extreme lengths, contributing to the MRCR cliff between 256K and 1M (Section 4).
- **Aggressive ~90% KV compression** at 1M could cause needle-in-haystack failures (per agent WCCFTech report, not independently fetched).
- The MRCR 0.59 at 1M figure [hf-blog] is consistent with this prediction; no controlled needle-in-haystack study has been published.

## 10. Price Instability (PRODUCTION SIGNAL, NOT A QUALITY BUG)

**Source:** [The Next Web, 2026-04-27](https://thenextweb.com/news/deepseek-v4-pro-price-cut-75-percent).

DeepSeek announced a **75% promotional discount on V4-Pro within 3 days of launch**, valid until May 5, 2026, alongside a 10× reduction in cache-hit input pricing across the API [tnw]. This is not a model failure but is a **production signal**: a 75% cut three days after release suggests over-provisioned launch pricing and that V4-Pro's stable production economics have not yet settled. Build cost models with this volatility in mind.
